title: Effect of perioperative electroacupuncture as an adjunctive therapy on postoperative analgesia with tramadol and ketamine in prostatectomy: a randomised sham-controlled single-blind trial
source_read: Complete9PDFpages via renderedimages, pp215–222 plus copyright page; Table1p218,Table2p220 visually checked. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01526525 official API read. SAGE supplemental URL failed; legacy BMJ supplement redirects to journal homepage403; main article available locally.
comparator: Nonpenetrating/no-current sham plus same drug regimen
denominator_source: p218Fig1,Table1; EA severe nausea/dizziness1,vomiting1; sham bleed/reoperation1,delirium1,severe nausea/dizziness1
population: Men50–75ASA1–3 radical retropubic prostatectomyGA, Thessaloniki; publicationJan–Dec2012
intervention: 100HzLI4bilateral30min at abdominal closure then4HzST36+LI4bilateral30min immediately after extubation
drug: Tramadol; additional rescue morphine; intraoperative remifentanil
pca_formulation: Not PCA: adjustable continuous infusion tramadol0.15mg/kg/h + ketamine0.15mg/kg/h following pre-end tramadol1.5mg/kg/ketamine10mg bolus30min before end. Max tramadol600mg24h;ketamine300mg24h.
rescue_regimen: IfNRS>3 orPPI≥2, tramadol50mgIV, then morphine2mgIV ifNRSfalls<2within30min; repeat. Sedation>2stop/reassess infusion. Parecoxib40mgIV andparacetamol20mg/kgIV pre-end.

results.window: Perioperative totals in table; postoperative-only boundary unresolved; excludes morphine as separate drug

results.outcome: Absent bowel sounds labelled absent bowel movement
results.qualification: Not flatus/defecation or continuous time-to-first bowel movement

results.format: Text reports reduction45min andtotal P<.001; exact mass/events unavailable in main article
